name: Phirni
ingredients: 1/2 cup basmati rice, soaked for 2 hours then drained
1 liter full-fat milk (preferably buffalo milk for richness)
1/2 cup sugar (or to taste; traditionalists use jaggery or date syrup)
1/4 cup heavy cream (optional, for extra richness)
10-12 threads saffron, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk
1 teaspoon cardamom powder (from freshly ground green pods)
2 tablespoons slivered almonds and pistachios for garnish
1 tablespoon rose water or kewra water (authentic floral touch)
1 tablespoon ghee (clarified butter, for roasting nuts)
instructions: 1. Rinse soaked rice, drain, and grind to a coarse paste with a few tablespoons of water. The texture should be slightly gritty, not smooth.
2. In a heavy-bottomed pan, bring milk to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring frequently to prevent scorching. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes, allowing volume to reduce slightly.

3. Add rice paste to the simmering milk in a thin stream, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Continue stirring for 15-20 minutes until mixture thickens and rice is fully cooked, coating the back of a spoon.
4. Stir in sugar until fully dissolved. Add saffron milk, cardamom powder, and rose water; mix well. If using cream, fold in gently for a silkier texture.
5. In a small pan, heat ghee and lightly roast slivered almonds and pistachios until golden. Set aside.

6. Pour phirni into earthenware bowls (kulhads) or serving dishes. Garnish with roasted nuts and a few saffron threads. Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours until chilled and set.
7. Serve cold, preferably in traditional clay pots, to enhance flavor.
description: A fragrant, creamy symphony of ground rice, cardamom, and saffron, steeped in the moonlit nostalgia of Punjabi harvest festivals.
